formation.title: Birth of the Ashanti Confederacy
formation.text:
Under the sacred shade of the kum tree, from which our capital takes its name, the scattered Akan chiefdoms have been forged into one confederacy. The priest Okomfo Anokye called down the Golden Stool from the heavens, and upon it the soul of our nation rests. The Denkyira overlords who once demanded tribute in gold and blood have been broken, and their vassal states now look to Kumasi.

But what kind of confederacy shall this be? The Golden Stool grants authority that transcends any single chief, a sacred mandate to unite all the Akan peoples under one spiritual authority. Yet the goldfields and trade routes that made this victory possible whisper of a different destiny: a commercial empire whose merchants bring the wealth of the world to Kumasi's broad streets.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Stool commands, and the nation obeys.

modifiers.name: Authority of the Golden Stool
modifiers.text: The Sika Dwa Kofi, the Golden Stool born on a Friday, descended from the heavens to sanctify the union of the Ashanti people. Its authority is absolute, no Asantehene sits upon it, but rules in its name. The nation's unity flows from this sacred symbol.

options.text: Gold speaks louder than any stool.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Gold Coast
modifiers.text: The wealth of the Ashanti Confederacy flows from the forest goldfields to the coastal forts, from the cola nut caravans to the northern markets. Kumasi sits at the heart of trade networks spanning from the Sahel to the Atlantic, turning gold dust into the currency of empire.

advances.name: Akan Clan System
advances.text: The matrilineal Akan clan structure, where inheritance and political succession pass through the mother's line, provides a stable foundation for confederate governance.

advances.name: Gold Dust Currency
advances.text: Akan gold dust serves as both currency and measure of wealth, weighed against standardized brass weights in every marketplace and court across the forest kingdoms.

advances.name: Forest Warfare Traditions
advances.text: The dense tropical forests of the Gold Coast demand a different kind of warrior, one who can move silently through the undergrowth, strike from ambush, and vanish before the enemy can respond.

advances.name: Cola Nut Trade
advances.text: The stimulant cola nut, grown in the southern forests, is traded northward across the savanna to Muslim communities where alcohol is forbidden, creating lucrative trade routes to the Sahel.

advances.name: Shrine Houses
advances.text: Elaborate shrine houses honor the ancestors and the powerful deities that protect the Akan peoples. These sacred spaces bind communities together through shared spiritual practice.

advances.name: Akan Metalworking
advances.text:
Akan goldsmiths and brass-casters produce exquisite regalia, goldweights, and ritual objects using the lost-wax casting technique passed down through generations of master craftsmen.

Available in: Brass Casters' Foundry

advances.name: Confederacy Founding
advances.text: The union of scattered Akan chiefdoms under the Golden Stool, forged through the defeat of the Denkyira overlords, marks the birth of the Ashanti Confederacy.

event.title: The Fall of Denkyira
event.text:
At the Battle of Feyiase in 1701, the combined forces of the Ashanti confederacy shattered the army of Denkyirahene Ntim Gyakari. The golden regalia of Denkyira, including the note of alliance with the Dutch at Elmina, fell into Ashanti hands. The gold mines, the coastal trade routes, and the subject peoples of Denkyira's empire now belong to the confederacy.

Ntim Gyakari himself was slain, and his skull would become a drinking vessel at the court of the Asantehene. The states that once bowed to Denkyira must now choose: will they be absorbed into an Ashanti military machine that rewards battlefield valor, or welcomed into a broader confederation that turns former enemies into loyal members?

options.text: Press the advantage; the conquered serve or they fall.

modifiers.name: Conquerors of Denkyira
modifiers.text: The army that broke Denkyira's chains carries the momentum of liberation. These veterans know the taste of victory against a superior foe.

options.text: Extend the stool's protection; former enemies become future allies.

modifiers.name: Confederate Unity
modifiers.text: The genius of the confederacy lies not in conquest alone but in integration, bringing defeated peoples into the fold as members, not subjects.

advances.name: The Golden Stool
advances.text: The Sika Dwa Kofi, the Golden Stool Born on Friday, descended from the heavens at the command of the priest Okomfo Anokye, embodying the spirit and unity of the Ashanti nation.

advances.name: Asafo Companies
advances.text: The asafo military companies, organized around chiefs and measured by their 'guns,' form the backbone of the Ashanti army, a structured force of musket-armed warriors fighting in coordinated formations.

advances.name: Kente Weaving
advances.text:
The intricate strip-woven kente cloth, produced by specialized weavers in villages like Bonwire, is reserved for royalty and serves as both art and political statement.

Available in: Kente Workshop

advances.name: Opoku Ware's Expansion
advances.text: Under Asantehene Opoku Ware, the confederacy expanded to its greatest territorial extent, conquering Bono, Wassa, Gonja, and Gyaman between 1723 and 1750.

event.title: The Conquests of Opoku Ware
event.text:
Asantehene Opoku Ware, who succeeded the great Osei Tutu, has carried the confederacy's banners further than any before him. The Bono kingdom fell in 1723, followed by Wassa in 1726. Western Gonja submitted in 1732, and Gyaman followed in 1740. By the end of his reign, the Ashanti Confederacy controls territory stretching across what will become modern Ghana and into the Ivory Coast, with three to five million people under its authority.

Opoku Ware also encouraged the expansion of craft production, establishing factories to innovate in weaving and metalwork. Under his patronage, the kente cloth tradition flourished, and Danish observers at the coast recorded their admiration for Ashanti craftsmanship.

options.text: The legacy of Opoku Ware endures.

advances.name: Royal Gold Mines
advances.text: Osei Tutu declared the gold mines royal possessions, ensuring that the wealth of the forest goldfields flowed directly to the Asantehene and fueled the expansion of the confederacy.

advances.name: Kumasi Palace Complex
advances.text: The sprawling royal palace at Kumasi, with its broad streets, courtyards, and more than sixty rooms, serves as the political and cultural heart of the confederacy.

advances.name: European Firearms Trade
advances.text: The Ashanti eagerly adopted European firearms, particularly the Long Dane musket, trading gold and captives for weapons that gave their armies devastating firepower.

advances.name: Goldweight Standards
advances.text:
The standardized brass goldweight system, combining Islamic, Portuguese, and local measurements, enables precise commercial transactions across the entire Akan trading world.

Available in: Brass Casters' Foundry

advances.name: Northern Trade Routes
advances.text: The great trade routes running north from Kumasi connect the forest zone to the Sahel, exchanging cola nuts, gold, and cloth for salt, livestock, shea butter, and imported goods.

advances.name: The Asantehemaa
advances.text: The Queen Mother shares responsibility for affairs of state, advising the Asantehene and holding the power to check his authority, a remarkable institution of shared governance.

advances.name: Craft Village Specialization
advances.text: Specialized craft villages surround Kumasi: Bonwire for cloth-weaving, Ntonso for cloth-dyeing, Pankrono for pottery, Ahwiaa for woodworking, and Breman for goldsmithing.

advances.name: Rolling Fire Tactics
advances.text: Ashanti musketeers advance in multiple lines, each discharging volleys and cycling to the rear to reload. This rolling fire technique maintains continuous pressure on the enemy.

advances.name: Coast Trade Relations
advances.text: Trade with European forts on the coast, first the Portuguese at Elmina, then the Dutch and British, brings firearms, textiles, and manufactured goods into the interior.

advances.name: Meritocratic Reforms
advances.text: Asantehene Osei Kwadwo replaced hereditary appointments with a merit-based system, transforming the Asokwafo hornblowers into a professional civil service academy.

event.title: The Reforms of Osei Kwadwo
event.text:
Asantehene Osei Kwadwo, who reigned from 1764 to 1777, has fundamentally transformed how the Ashanti state governs itself. Where once hereditary chiefs filled every position of consequence, Kwadwo instituted a radical principle: appointment by ability rather than birth.

The Asokwafo, originally a troop of royal hornblowers, has been transformed into an academy for the education and training of future government officials. The most talented young men from across the confederacy are recruited into the Asokwafo community, trained in administration, diplomacy, and statecraft, and then deployed wherever the empire needs them.

But not everyone welcomes this transformation. The hereditary chiefs see their traditional prerogatives being stripped away, and they warn that meritocracy without lineage produces officials with no loyalty to anything but their own advancement.

options.text: Ability alone determines a man's place.

modifiers.name: Kwadwo's Meritocracy
modifiers.text: Osei Kwadwo replaced birth with ability as the measure of a man's worth in government. The Asokwafo, once mere royal hornblowers, now serve as a training ground for the empire's finest administrators.

options.text: Custom and lineage are the foundation of order.

modifiers.name: Hereditary Stability
modifiers.text: The traditional chiefs and their lineages provide the bedrock of Ashanti governance. Their authority, rooted in clan and custom, ensures continuity through the generations.

advances.name: Asokwafo Civil Service
advances.text: The Asokwafo, transformed from royal musicians into a civil service training school, produces administrators appointed by ability rather than birth.

advances.name: Osei Bonsu's Army
advances.text: Under Osei Bonsu, the Ashanti army was modernized with improved firearms, better organization, and tactics capable of defeating European-led forces.

advances.name: Provincial Administration
advances.text: The four-tier system of state, district, village, and lineage governance, administered by the imperial bureaucracy in Kumasi, ensures effective control across the confederacy.

advances.name: Bantama Mausoleum
advances.text: The Bantama royal mausoleum at Kumasi houses the remains of past Asantehenes, its thick walls marked with royal symbols, a sacred site connecting the living to the authority of the ancestors.

advances.name: Odwira Festival
advances.text: The annual Odwira purification festival renews the bonds between the Asantehene, the chiefs, and the people, reaffirming the spiritual foundations of the confederacy.

advances.name: Gold Coast Dominance
advances.text: The Ashanti Confederacy's control of the interior goldfields and trade routes to the coast makes it the dominant power on the Gold Coast.

advances.name: Anglo-Ashanti Resistance
advances.text: The war with the British that began in 1823 tested the confederacy against the world's foremost imperial power. The Ashanti won its first great battle, killing a British governor, and held the forest against every march on Kumasi.

event.title: The Anglo-Ashanti Wars
event.text:
The British have pushed inland from their coastal forts, claiming the protection of the Fante and the other peoples of the Gold Coast. Under Asantehene Osei Bonsu, the Ashanti answered with force. In 1824, Sir Charles MacCarthy led a British and allied force against the Ashanti at Nsamankow and was utterly defeated; his skull was taken as a gold-rimmed drinking cup by the Asantehene.

But the British returned with greater numbers and new weapons. In 1826, on the plain of Katamanso near Accra, their rockets and the massed allies of the coast broke the Ashanti army in the open field.

The confederacy faces an existential choice: dig deeper into the forest and fight a war of attrition that plays to traditional Ashanti strengths, or adapt to the enemy's methods and build the capacity to meet them on modern terms.

options.text: The forest is our weapon. Let them bleed for every mile.

modifiers.name: Defiant Resistance
modifiers.text: The forest is our fortress. Every tree conceals a musketeer, every path leads to ambush. Let the invaders learn that the Ashanti do not kneel.

options.text: Learn from the enemy to surpass the enemy.

modifiers.name: Pragmatic Adaptation
modifiers.text: The world changes, and the wise nation changes with it. Adopt what makes the enemy strong (their discipline, their fortifications, their methods) and turn it against them.

advances.name: Professional Standing Army
advances.text: The transition from clan-based levies to a professional standing army gives the Ashanti Confederacy a permanent military force capable of rapid deployment.

advances.name: Kumasi Urbanization
advances.text: Kumasi's broad streets, planned quarters, and extensive infrastructure make it one of the great cities of West Africa, a center of commerce, governance, and culture.

advances.name: Gold Refining
advances.text:
Advanced techniques for purifying and refining gold dust increase the value of the confederacy's primary export and strengthen its position in international trade.

Available in: Brass Casters' Foundry

advances.name: Judicial Reform
advances.text: The centralization of the court system under the Asantehene as supreme judge creates a unified legal framework across the confederacy's diverse communities.

advances.name: Imperial Road Network
advances.text: A network of maintained roads radiating from Kumasi enables rapid military deployment, efficient trade, and effective communication across the confederacy's vast territory.

advances.name: War of the Golden Stool
advances.text: When the king of Gyaman had a golden stool made in the likeness of the Golden Stool, Osei Bonsu marched north in 1818, broke Gyaman and had the copy melted down. The nation takes the field as one when the Stool is slighted.

event.title: The Stool of Gyaman
event.text:
Word has come to Kumasi that Kwadwo Adinkra, king of Gyaman in the north-west and a tributary of the Asantehene, has had a stool of gold made for himself in the likeness of the Golden Stool. There can be no second seat for the soul of a nation. To copy the Stool is to claim what it holds.

Osei Bonsu has called out the army of the confederacy and marched on Gyaman. Adinkra has been defeated and killed, his kingdom brought back under tribute, and his golden stool carried to Kumasi. There it has been melted down, and the gold cast into two masks that now hang from the Golden Stool itself.

options.text: There is one Golden Stool.

advances.name: Kola Trade
advances.text:
With the slave ships leaving the coast, the Ashanti turn north. Kola from the forest is carried to the market of Salaga and sold to the caravans of Hausaland, where the nut is prized above every other gift.

Available in: Kola Grove

advances.name: Cultural Preservation
advances.text: Through war and peace alike the Ashanti keep their institutions: the stool system, kente weaving, goldwork, and the Odwira festival endure as living traditions.

advances.name: Modern Governance
advances.text: The adaptation of traditional confederate governance to modern institutional frameworks, preserving the Asantehene's authority within a contemporary administrative structure.

advances.name: Modern Ashanti Army
advances.text: A fully modernized military force that combines traditional Ashanti fighting spirit with contemporary organization, equipment, and tactics.

advances.name: Osei Bonsu's Diplomacy
advances.text: Asantehene Osei Bonsu received the British missions of 1817 and 1820 at Kumasi and bound them by written treaty. Muslim scribes from the north kept his letters and accounts, and strangers of many nations lived under his protection in the capital.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Ashanti
destiny.text: The Ashanti Confederacy has been forged, but its ultimate shape remains to be decided. The Golden Stool grants authority; the goldfields grant wealth. Both paths lead to greatness.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Ashanti Destiny
event.text: The confederacy stands at the threshold of greatness. Whether through the authority of the Golden Stool or the power of gold dust, the Ashanti shall leave their mark upon the world. The path we have chosen will define the nation for generations to come.

options.text: Our destiny awaits.

destiny.name: Wars of the Stool
destiny.text: The Golden Stool demands submission. Bring the northern kingdoms under Ashanti authority by conquering Dagbon and its trading center of Salaga. Accumulate 1000 gold to fund the campaign.

conditions.text: Chose Authority of the Golden Stool
Stability at least 25
Own Yendi, or a subject owns it
Own Salaga, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: Dagbon Submits
event.text: The northern kingdom of Dagbon has fallen to Ashanti arms. Yendi, seat of the Ya-Na, now acknowledges the authority of the Golden Stool. The great trading center of Salaga, where cola nuts and gold are exchanged for salt and livestock, is ours. The confederacy's military reach now extends beyond the forest into the savanna.

options.text: The Stool's authority grows.

destiny.name: Great Ashanti
destiny.text: The confederacy must project its power beyond the forest belt. Conquer Oyo-Ile, the Yoruba capital, and the Borgu stronghold of Nikki. The asafo companies must be organized, and prestige kept above 50.

conditions.text: Own Ọ̀yọ́ Ile, or a subject owns it
Own Nikki, or a subject owns it
Renaissance or later
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Greater Ashanti
event.text:
Ashanti armies have marched far beyond the forest homeland. Oyo-Ile, the great Yoruba capital, has fallen, and the Borgu warriors have submitted. The confederacy now controls territory stretching across the entire Guinea coast hinterland.

This expansion demands a choice. We can build a war machine that mobilizes quickly and overwhelms opponents through speed and numbers, or we can establish a garrison state with fortified positions, intelligence networks, and the diplomatic leverage to strike when the moment is right.

options.text: Speed and overwhelming force.

modifiers.name: Ashanti War Machine
modifiers.text: The confederacy's military apparatus has been transformed into a rapid-response war machine. Supply lines are extended, garrisons reinforced, and new regiments raised with terrifying speed.

options.text: Fortification and intelligence.

modifiers.name: Ashanti Garrison State
modifiers.text: A network of fortified positions and spy networks gives the Ashanti Confederacy the intelligence and strategic patience to choose the perfect moment to strike.

destiny.name: Ashanti Imperium
destiny.text: Build an empire that stretches from the Sahara to the sea. Conquer Timbuktu, Benin, and Niani. The army must carry European firearms, with 3000 gold in the treasury and prestige above 75.

conditions.text: Own Timbuktu, or a subject owns it
Own Benin, or a subject owns it
Own Niani, or a subject owns it
Discovery or later
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Ashanti Imperium
event.text:
From Timbuktu in the Sahel to Benin on the coast, from Niani in the west to the eastern forests, the Ashanti Imperium stretches across a vast swathe of West Africa. No power on the continent can match the armies that march under the Golden Stool's banner.

But how shall this imperium be governed? Through terror and overwhelming military force that crushes all resistance, or through a more measured approach that rebuilds conquered lands and turns enemies into productive subjects?

options.text: Let them fear the name Ashanti.

modifiers.name: Terror of the Ashanti
modifiers.text: The very name Ashanti strikes fear into neighboring peoples. Mercenaries flock to the banner, and fortified cities fall before the assault. But endless conquest strains the treasury.

options.text: Rebuild what war has broken.

modifiers.name: Pax Ashanti
modifiers.text: The Ashanti Imperium rebuilds what war has broken. Conquered peoples are resettled, cities reconstructed, and diplomats dispatched to ensure the peace holds.

destiny.name: Lords of the Coast
destiny.text: Seize control of the western Gold Coast by taking Axim and Apollonia in Nzima territory. These coastal positions give direct access to European trade. Accumulate 1000 gold.

conditions.text: Chose Lords of the Gold Coast
Stability at least 25
Own Axim, or a subject owns it
Own Apollonia, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Coast Is Ours
event.text: The western Gold Coast is now firmly under Ashanti control. Axim and Apollonia in Nzima territory give the confederacy direct access to the European trading posts. No longer must Ashanti merchants rely on middlemen to reach the ships at anchor. Gold dust flows directly from the mines to the coastal warehouses.

options.text: Gold flows from forest to sea.

destiny.name: The Golden Trade
destiny.text: Make the confederacy the house of gold in West Africa. Build gold treasuries in three towns where gold dust is weighed and counted, accumulate 2000 gold, ensure ivory flows through your markets, and maintain prestige above 50.

conditions.text: Owns a location with
Gold at least 2000
A market the country is in

children.text: Ivory is produced in the market
Ivory is traded in the market

conditions.text: Prestige at least 50

event.title: Masters of the Golden Trade
event.text:
The Ashanti Confederacy keeps its gold dust in treasuries in three towns, weighed and counted against the brass weights of the state, and has established itself as the financial heart of West Africa. Ivory, gold, cola nuts, and cloth flow through markets where Ashanti merchants set the prices. The confederacy's wealth is no longer measured only in gold dust but in the sophisticated instruments of international commerce.

Shall we open our ports to all comers, welcoming any ship that brings goods to trade and expanding our commercial reach across the seas? Or shall we cultivate a merchant aristocracy, a class of elite traders with the diplomatic connections and financial resources to dominate regional commerce?

options.text: Open the ports to the world.

modifiers.name: Open Ports Policy
modifiers.text: Ashanti ports welcome ships from across the world. Devastated coastal areas recover quickly, and the confederacy's commercial reach extends to distant shores.

options.text: Cultivate our merchant princes.

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes of Kumasi
modifiers.text: An elite class of Ashanti merchant-diplomats maintains commercial relationships across the region, though their focus on trade comes at some cost to military readiness.

destiny.name: Empire of Gold
destiny.text: Build the wealthiest state in West Africa. Conquer Djenne to control the trans-Saharan trade terminus, raise Kumasi from a forest village into a city, put Ashanti merchants to work in four markets along the northern roads, amass 3000 gold, and reach prestige 75.

conditions.text: Own Djenné, or a subject owns it
Kumasi is owned and has grown into a city
Num of markets with merchants at least 4
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Empire of Gold
event.text:
Djenne has fallen. The trans-Saharan trade terminus, where gold from the forest meets salt from the desert and goods from across the Islamic world, is now an Ashanti possession. The confederacy's commercial network spans from the Atlantic coast to the edge of the Sahara, from the forest goldfields to the great markets of the Sahel.

This is the apex of Ashanti commercial power. Shall the empire embrace its diverse peoples and faiths, building a cosmopolitan trading civilization that welcomes all? Or shall it invest its gold in ships and naval power, projecting Ashanti influence across the seas?

options.text: A thousand peoples under one golden roof.

modifiers.name: Cosmopolitan Empire
modifiers.text: The Ashanti commercial empire embraces traders and settlers of all faiths. This open society, backed by naval power, projects influence far beyond West Africa.

options.text: Build a fleet worthy of our wealth.

modifiers.name: Golden Fleet
modifiers.text: Ashanti gold funds a fleet of trading vessels and warships. Shipyards work at a furious pace, though the investment diverts resources from the land army.

units.name: Akan Forest Skirmishers
units.text: Light warriors trained in the dense tropical forests of the Gold Coast. They move silently through the undergrowth, striking from ambush before melting back into the trees.

units.name: Asafo Musketeers
units.text: Musket-armed warriors organized into asafo companies under their chiefs. They carry their guns at the same angle and fire volleys on command, combining traditional clan loyalty with firearms discipline.

units.name: Dane Gun Infantry
units.text: Ashanti soldiers armed with the Long Dane, the preferred European trade musket, trained in the rolling fire technique that earned the respect of European observers.

units.name: Bonsu Guard
units.text: The elite guard of Asantehene Osei Bonsu, battle-hardened veterans who defeated a British governor and carried his skull as a trophy. Their morale is unshakeable.

units.name: Ashanti Professional Infantry
units.text: Full-time soldiers of the Ashanti standing army, maintained year-round rather than raised seasonally. They represent the confederacy's military evolution from clan levies to professional force.

units.name: Modern Ashanti Infantry
units.text: The final evolution of Ashanti military tradition, modern soldiers who inherit the fighting spirit of Osei Tutu's warriors and the organizational discipline of Osei Bonsu's reforms.

buildings.name: Gold Treasury
buildings.text: A royal depository where gold dust is received, weighed against standardized brass goldweights, and stored. It serves as both treasury and commercial center.

buildings.name: Asante Shrine House
buildings.text: An elaborate shrine house built in the traditional Asante wattle-and-daub style, with intricate wall decorations honoring powerful deities and ancestral spirits.

buildings.name: Stool House
buildings.text: A sacred repository housing the clan stools that embody the soul of each chiefdom. The most important houses the Golden Stool itself, the spiritual center of the confederacy.

buildings.name: Kente Workshop
buildings.text: A specialized weaving workshop where master weavers produce kente cloth, strip-woven textiles of silk and cotton in patterns and colors reserved for royalty and the elite.

buildings.name: Asante Palace Complex
buildings.text: A sprawling royal complex in the Kumasi style, with broad courtyards, thatched-roof chambers, and extensive wall decorations that astonished European visitors.

buildings.name: Trade Lodge
buildings.text: A waystation on the northern trade routes where Ashanti merchants exchange cola nuts, gold, and cloth for salt, livestock, and goods from across the Sahel.

buildings.name: Asokwafo Academy
buildings.text: A training school for the meritocratic civil service, where talented young men from across the confederacy learn administration, diplomacy, and statecraft.

buildings.name: Royal Mausoleum
buildings.text: A Bantama-style burial complex with thick walls marked by royal symbols, housing the remains of past Asantehenes in a solemn space meant for reflection and ancestral communion.

buildings.name: Imperial Road Station
buildings.text: A rest stop and toll collection point on the road network radiating from Kumasi, facilitating both military movement and commercial traffic across the confederacy.

buildings.name: Kola Grove
buildings.text: A grove of kola trees in the forest zone, tended by the villages that own it. The trees are weeded, pruned and shaded, and the land where kola grows bears more of it for the road north.

where.text: The location's raw material is Medicaments

buildings.name: Brass Casters' Foundry
buildings.text: A brass casters' workshop, where skilled artisans cast kuduo vessels, gold weights, and ceremonial objects using the lost-wax technique.

buildings.name: Craft Village
buildings.text: A village near Kumasi that keeps a single craft for the court. Pankrono is known for its pottery and Ahwiaa for its carved stools.

buildings.name: Ashanti War Council
buildings.text: The supreme military council of the Ashanti Imperium, where the greatest generals of the confederacy plan campaigns that span from the Sahara to the sea.

buildings.name: Great Market of Kumasi
buildings.text: The legendary central market of Kumasi, where gold dust, ivory, cola nuts, kente cloth, and goods from across the world change hands under the watchful eye of royal trade officials.

list.name: Asantemanhyiamu
list.text: At Odwira each year the Asantehene convened the Asantemanhyiamu, the national assembly of the amanhene: the paramount chiefs of the constituent Akan states (Mampong, Dwaben, Bekwai, Kokofu, Nsuta, Kumawu, and others added by conquest). The assembly ratified declarations of war, confirmed successions, arbitrated disputes between omans, and approved the levy quotas each district would supply. Its authority rested on the founding compact of c.1701 by which Osei Tutu's confederates had pooled sovereignty under the Sika Dwa Kofi while keeping their hereditary stools. It was the kingdom's federal constitution: without its consent no Asantehene could compel the chiefs.

list.name: Nhenkwaa Palace Household
list.text: The Nhenkwaa were a permanent caste of palace servants attached directly to the Asantehene at Manhyia: gun-bearers (atumtufo), drummers (akyeremade), horn-blowers (asokwafo), executioners (abrafo), and the sumankwafo who maintained the throne's protective talismans. Recruited largely from war captives and the unfree, they stood outside the matrilineal clan structure and owed everything to the king; many rose to be confidential agents and ambassadors. By making the palace household a self-contained executive, Opoku Ware (r.1720-1750) and Osei Kwadwo (r.1764-1777) bypassed the amanhene and built a state apparatus that could function without the chiefs' consent.

conditions.text: Own Kumasi, or a subject owns it

list.name: Akwantufo Road Wardens
list.text: Eight great roads radiated from Kumasi to the frontier provinces, hewn through the rainforest and maintained as the arteries of the Confederacy. Each was patrolled by akwanmofo wardens under the akwansrafohene, with toll-keepers (nkwansrafo) at every oman frontier levying duties on cola nuts, kente, gold, captives, salt, and European trade goods. Bowdich's 1817 embassy described a pavement of beaten earth kept clear of vegetation, a sophisticated public-works system unique among the Guinea Coast kingdoms. The roads doubled as the levy-call infrastructure: the atumtufo standard travelling down each road mustered the districts along it.

list.name: Daban Gold-Dust Treasury
list.text: Gold dust (sika futuro) was the Confederacy's currency, weighed against brass abrammuo weights cast in geometric and figurative forms. The Daban (the royal treasury at Manhyia) was administered by the Gyaasewahene as chief treasurer, with the Sanaahene as deputy and the fotosanfohene inspecting weights at every market. A national standard of abrammuo made long-distance trade between Akan markets possible without dispute, and all gold mined in the kingdom owed a royal share to the strongrooms. Bowdich saw piles of dust kept in elephant-skin sacks that he estimated at hundreds of pounds of gold per chamber.

list.name: Kotoko Council and Adamfo
list.text: The Kotoko was the inner war council of the Asantehene, named for the porcupine ('if you kill a thousand, a thousand will come') that was the kingdom's emblem. It comprised the great captains (the Bantamahene as senior commander, the Adontenhene of the vanguard, the Nifahene of the right wing, the Benkumhene of the left, the Kyidomhene of the rear), meeting under the Bogyawe tree. Parallel to it ran the adamfo system: each tributary and each foreign power was assigned a 'royal friend' at Kumasi who handled all its diplomatic traffic and was personally liable for any dispute. Together they gave Ashanti a professionalized war-and-embassy apparatus unmatched on the Guinea Coast.
